name: Refugee Status (Refugees Act 2006)

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution on grounds of race, nationality, religion, sex, political opinion, or membership of a particular social group (1951 UN Convention), or compelled to leave due to external aggression, occupation, foreign domination, or events seriously disturbing public order (1969 OAU Convention).
Application submitted within 30 days of entering Uganda.

outcome.duration_length: indefinite, subject to settlement/registration status; identity cards and travel documents issued

sources.title: Refugee Law Project, School of Law, Makerere University, Uganda -- The Refugees Act 2006 Factsheet: eligibility under the 1951 UN Convention and 1969 OAU Convention definitions; applications within 30 days of entry, 90-day decision window; rights to identity cards, travel documents, freedom of movement, gainful employment in one's chosen profession, agriculture/commerce/industry rights, education access, trade-union association, religious freedom; administered by the Office of the Prime Minister's Department of Refugees (Commissioner for Refugees) with an Eligibility Committee and a Refugee Appeals Board (30-day appeal window)

Office of the Prime Minister, Uganda -- CRRF Statement: confirms Uganda's 'progressive refugee model' operationally -- land allocation for farming and shelter, open borders, non-camp policy in most settlements, right to work, equal access to government social services, described as among the most generous refugee policies in the world

Office of the Prime Minister, Uganda -- Refugee Settlements: administering structure (Department of Refugees under OPM, Commissioner for Refugees, four Regional Desk Offices, Settlement Commandants), confirms refugees may also settle independently in urban areas like Kampala rather than only in settlements

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Uganda). STATUS: DRAFT -- the precise statutory eligibility test and procedural timelines (30-day application window, 90-day decision, Eligibility Committee, Refugee Appeals Board) are sourced only to a tier-2 academic factsheet (Refugee Law Project, Makerere University School of Law); no tier-1 Ugandan-government-hosted copy of the Refugees Act 2006's operative text itself was located in this build, so the file stays draft per this dataset's rule despite strong tier-1 corroboration of the surrounding operational reality. SUBSTANTIVELY, THIS IS ONE OF THE STRONGEST AND MOST GENUINELY DOCUMENTED HUMANITARIAN ROUTES IN THIS ENTIRE DATASET: Uganda's Office of the Prime Minister -- Uganda's own government, tier-1 -- directly confirms land allocation for farming and shelter, a non-camp/open-border policy in most locations, full right to work, and access to government social services on par with citizens, widely regarded internationally as one of the most generous refugee policies anywhere. This stands in sharp contrast to Bahrain (no framework at all) and Bangladesh (large-scale protection administered through pure administrative discretion under a colonial alien-control statute with no refugee-specific law) built earlier in this dataset -- Uganda has both a purpose-built statute (Refugees Act 2006) AND documented, functioning rights delivery, but the statute's own text simply wasn't independently locatable at tier-1 in this build. work_rights and study_rights are marked 'full' based on the tier-1 OPM operational confirmation, a deliberate departure from this dataset's usual practice of defaulting to 'restricted' for humanitarian routes when direct legal-text confirmation is thin, because here the OPERATIONAL reality (not just the statutory text) is independently tier-1 confirmed.
